item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump Downplays Uranium Threat, Sending More Conflicting Signals
item.summary: President Trump told Reuters he was no longer worried about Iran’s uranium stockpile because it is “so far underground” and can be monitored by spy satellites. He was set to deliver a speech at 9 p.m. Eastern.

item.title: Israel’s Message to a Broad Swath of Lebanon: Shiites Must Go
item.summary: Israel has issued sweeping evacuation warnings, and pressed some Christian and Druse leaders to expel Shiite Muslims from southern towns, the leaders said.

item.title: The Sailors Stranded in the Persian Gulf
item.summary: Thousands of civilian sailors have been stranded for more than a month in waters surrounded by a conflict zone because of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: French Prosecutors Link Foiled Attack on American Bank to a Pro-Iranian Group
item.summary: The group is suspected of involvement in a string of attacks on Jewish targets in Belgium, Britain and the Netherlands.

item.title: 29 Killed in Russian Military Plane Crash in Crimea
item.summary: Investigators cited a possible technical malfunction.

item.title: Europe Has a ‘Guns vs. Butter’ Problem. War in Iran Makes It Worse.
item.summary: After decades of prioritizing domestic over military spending, the continent’s leaders are trying to pivot. That is straining national budgets and could anger voters.

item.title: Heavy bombings across Tehran jolt its war-weary residents.
item.summary: Some people in the capital said the blasts on Wednesday morning were among the most powerful they had felt in more than a month of war.

item.title: Why Reopening the Strait of Hormuz Matters for the U.S. Economy
item.summary: The interconnectedness of global energy markets means that the effects of Iran’s blockade of the waterway are not limited to countries directly dependent on oil from the Middle East.

item.title: Netanyahu makes the case that wars on Iran have succeeded.
item.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed that Israel had crushed Iran’s capacity to make nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles. But Iran has continued attacking Israel and Persian Gulf countries and is believed to still have highly enriched uranium.

item.title: In UK Prisons, Drones Fly In Contraband ‘As if by Uber Eats’
item.summary: Decades-old prison buildings were designed to be secure from the ground but not the air. Experts say that makes a lucrative smuggling trade hard to tackle.
